sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: For a 3D-printing engineering elective, I built a Darksaber hilt that I could keep, use, and continue improving. The project brought together Fusion 360 modeling, printed components, lighting, and a modular assembly.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The main challenge was fitting electronics into a handheld shell without exposing them or weakening the print. Small details had to remain readable at the scale of the finished object while allowing enough clearance for assembly.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: I measured reference imagery, blocked out the major forms, and hollowed the body for an electronics insert. Repeated prints helped refine the fit between the handle, guard, and lighting components. Editable dimensions made small clearance changes easier to carry through the model.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Black and gray surfaces emphasize the angular hilt and its repeated grooves. LEDs behind white acrylic create a diffused glow, while removable parts make repairs and later changes possible without rebuilding the entire object.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: I developed Dracula, a display typeface presented through a Transylvania-themed specimen. The project explores how a limited set of modular shapes can form a consistent alphabet with a distinct Gothic character.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The goal was to combine thin, restrained letterforms with older serif details and curved shapes. FontStruct’s block-based construction made curved transitions and a consistent relationship between uppercase and lowercase letters the main challenges.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Hand-drawn studies established the alphabet’s direction before digital trials tested the same features across different letters. Revisions focused on keeping the curves, stems, and decorative details related throughout the character set.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: The final specimen uses red, dark backgrounds, and castle imagery to connect the lettering to its Dracula theme. The contrast supports the typeface’s narrow forms while giving the alphabet a setting that reinforces its personality.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This menu redesign brings Omega Burger’s handheld and wall menus into one visual system. The project addresses inconsistent layouts while giving each format a role that fits how people read and order from it.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The handheld menu needed clear categories and room for detailed information. The wall menu had to work at a distance, with stronger illustration and a hierarchy that makes the main choices easy to find.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Site observations, visual research, and successive compositions informed the redesign. Layout trials explored the balance between food categories, supporting information, and illustration, followed by revisions and print checks.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Blue, red, and yellow connect the menus, while line illustrations referencing Greek architecture give the system a recognizable character. Repeated typography and category treatments create continuity across the different sizes.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: I created a personal identity that reflects my interest in vector work and clean line art. The mark is designed to feel approachable and memorable while remaining simple enough to carry across different applications.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The challenge was to find a balance between a refined, sophisticated identity and a more relaxed, bubbly personality. Curves, folds, and color needed to add character without making the mark feel crowded.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: A broad set of hand-drawn thumbnails led to a smaller group of tighter directions. I refined the shapes and relationships, then developed a palette, typography choices, patterns, and application studies around the selected mark.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: The final identity follows a less-is-more approach. Rounded lines and folded forms establish the mark’s personality, while the supporting color and pattern system give it flexibility beyond the logo itself.

sections.heading: MY ROLE & CONTRIBUTIONS
sections.text: My contributions included early logo drafts and sketches; typography, color, and moodboard explorations; field and visual research; and the social-media post series. I also contributed to the installation concept and 3D model with a teammate, developing the temple form and interactive elements. I produced printed proofs, compared layouts and image treatment, and refined spacing, type, saturation, and color balance with the group.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This collaborative rebrand concept explored how BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir could feel contemporary and inviting without losing its cultural identity. The group developed a connected visual system spanning logo treatments, typography, color, photography, promotional assets, and an installation concept. My focus was on helping establish the visual direction and carrying it through the social-media and spatial applications.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The challenge was balancing a fresh visual identity with the Mandir’s cultural and spiritual significance. The work needed to feel welcoming to a contemporary audience while remaining recognizable and meaningful to older visitors. A consistent identity had to hold together across small-format posts, banners, photography, and a larger installation, without making every application identical.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: My development began with field research and moodboards studying architecture, color, imagery, and typography. Logo sketches translated temple silhouettes into simplified marks, while type studies tested different ways to balance bold display lettering with culturally relevant forms. Printed social-media proofs made it easier to compare the spacing, text, shapes, and image treatment side by side. Feedback from those proofs led to refinements in saturation and color balance with the group.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: For the social-media series, I repeated a border shape and pattern to connect the posts while varying imagery, marks, and content for different messages. Layered lotus imagery, contrasting colors, and coordinated photo treatment extended the shared system. In the installation work, I developed the temple model with enlarged steps and an open doorway to feel inviting and monumental. Tapered openings suggested greater depth, while reduced detail in seating areas made those spaces appear more approachable. The result presented the same visual identity across both a digital post series and a physical-space concept.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: I made a cohesive set of handmade books inspired by Quentin Tarantino films as a gift for my dad. Each cover translates a recognizable scene into simplified shapes and color, while each binding responds to the character of its film.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The project combined visual consistency with the demands of physical construction. Cutting, measuring, gluing, and stitching needed careful planning so the books could work as individual objects and as a collection.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: The set explores chain stitch, three- and five-hole pamphlets, hardcover construction, Japanese stab binding, and Coptic binding. Moving between these methods helped me understand how structure changes both the process and the finished object.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Reduced illustrations and repeated color relationships tie the covers together. The varied bindings make the physical construction part of the concept, adding another way to distinguish each film while preserving the set’s shared identity.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This poster promotes Everybody through a figure whose identity remains deliberately open. The composition brings the play’s themes into a clear event poster aimed at a Chapman student audience.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The central challenge was to suggest a person without making the figure too specific. The poster also needed to balance an expressive concept with an information hierarchy that keeps the title and event details legible.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Thumbnails, moodboards, and tighter compositions explored the relationship between the head, repeated title, and supporting information. Revisions narrowed the direction toward a wireframe figure and a more controlled arrangement of type.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Purple introduces mystery, yellow establishes emphasis, and white supports the information. The repeated title fades through the composition, while the wireframe head creates an anonymous figure that can stand for anybody.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This wine-label and advertising concept develops a connected direction for three Norton wines. Sailing imagery and a shared visual language bring the bottles together as a family while leaving room for each label to feel distinct.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The labels needed to communicate a sense of elegance and relaxation, then extend into an advertisement that could hold the same atmosphere. Color and contrast had to work both on the bottle and in a larger composition.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Moodboards led into thumbnail studies, refined label directions, and bottle compositions. Advertisement trials tested how the product imagery could connect to the sailing theme before the final layout was resolved.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Desaturated hues and illustrative references to sailing and mythology establish the tone. The advertisement carries that direction through the line “Set Sail Towards Greatness,” connecting the visual setting to the bottle family.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: The Uncomfortable Cycle of Appropriation is an exhibition concept for the Guggenheim Gallery. It uses Aladdin as a point of departure to explore how representations can repeat and pass between generations.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The challenge was to translate an abstract cultural issue into a spatial experience within a limited footprint. The layout needed to guide visitors through the idea rather than relying entirely on explanatory text.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Research imagery, sketches, and model studies informed the exhibition’s sequence and arrangement. Interior compositions tested how the installation could create a contained narrative and direct attention through the proposed space.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: The final renders describe an educational installation centered on repetition and an uncomfortable cycle. The design uses the physical arrangement to connect the subject, the viewer’s movement, and the idea of recurring representation.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: I developed a connected Home, About, and Services website for AOMedia. The project focuses on making the business, its work, and the next step for an interested visitor easier to understand across desktop and mobile layouts.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The website needed a coherent structure that could present different types of information without feeling disconnected. A clear hierarchy, consistent cards, and visible contact points were central goals.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: The process included interviews, competitor research, personas, and a heuristic review, followed by hand-drawn wireframes and low-fidelity layouts. Digital revisions refined the grid and the relationship between content sections.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: AOMedia’s red anchors the visual system. Rounded forms and glass-like surfaces give the layouts a friendly character, while repeated grids and cards provide a consistent framework across the three pages.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This Encino app concept gathers local information into Home, Calendar, Info, Community, and Profile areas. It brings weather, events, local history, photos, and community content into a connected mobile experience.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The main challenge was organizing a dense set of city information without making the interface difficult to navigate. The design needed to separate different kinds of content while preserving a consistent structure between screens.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Design-thinking exercises, hand-drawn screens, moodboards, and low-fidelity layouts informed the organization. Revisions explored grouping, navigation, and how the app could move between practical information and a more personal view of the city.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Natural colors, rounded shapes, and soft gradients create a modern but nostalgic tone. The visual direction uses the Gelato Luxe reference as a starting point, then carries related hierarchy and spacing across the app’s main sections.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: Salus Vitae is a smart-ring brand concept developed through an identity system, brand book, website, social content, and advertising. The project explores how one visual direction can hold together across product communication and digital applications.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The challenge was maintaining consistency across a broad set of deliverables. The logo, typography, color, layout, and campaign imagery needed to work together without making every format look identical.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Research and moodboards informed logo sketches and refinements, followed by brand-book studies. Website sketches and wireframes developed the digital structure, while separate composition studies explored social and advertising applications.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: The final system repeats its core identity across editorial layouts, product-focused web pages, and campaign material. A shared visual structure links the different formats while allowing the content and emphasis to change.

salus-vitae.credit: Selected website background, social, and advertising imagery is AI-assisted, as disclosed in the project process book.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This portrait series develops a visual language for a personal avatar and a related portrait. Color and monochrome versions explore how the same approach can remain recognizable while changing its palette and emphasis.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: I wanted the avatar to feel expressive without fixing it to one obvious emotion. A three-quarter view and deliberately ambiguous expression became ways to suggest personality while keeping the first impression open.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Art Deco, abstraction, and Neo-Pop informed the direction, with Mondrian’s primary colors and Basquiat’s energy among the references. Compositions and digital revisions tested how far the faces could be simplified while retaining their character.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Block-like shapes, strong color relationships, and reduced features connect the portraits. The monochrome treatment tests that structure without relying on color, while the related portrait extends the same language to another subject.

princess-cake.context: GD 309 · Course concept for Valhalla Bakery

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This three-poster campaign presents Princess Cake through three qualities: elegant, beautiful, and delicate. Each illustration uses a different bird to express one of those qualities while keeping the cake at the center of the campaign.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The posters needed to feel like a family without repeating the same scene. The goal was to communicate the cake’s character through illustration, balancing a recognizable product with a more atmospheric and expressive setting.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Thumbnails and moodboards led into coordinated compositions and individual bird studies. Revisions refined the swan, peacock, and hummingbird posters, using a shared format and a directional composition to lead attention toward the cake.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Midcentury and Art Deco references inform the shapes, color, and typography. The swan suggests elegance, the peacock beauty, and the hummingbird delicacy. Related pastel colors and a consistent typographic structure connect all three posters.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: For this spring illustration, I chose a fig as a personal connection to growing and ripening fruit. The finished image pairs a whole fig with a cut half, creating a compact illustration that can work on its own or in a small application.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The image needed to remain recognizable through simplified shapes while retaining enough texture to feel rich and tactile. It also had to work beyond a single composition, including print and sticker-sized uses.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: The project moved from early spring concepts into fruit sketches, flat-color compositions, and digital revisions. The final direction focused on the contrast between the fig’s exterior and its exposed interior.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Purple, red, and yellow separate the skin and flesh, while stippled texture adds depth to the flat forms. A clean silhouette makes the illustration adaptable to small printed applications without requiring a fixed background.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: I translated the shipping-container imagery of Chromakopia into a small collectible. The piece combines a container and hanging mask, bringing the visual atmosphere of the music video into a physical object.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The main challenge was balancing recognizable proportions with a stylized interpretation. The finish needed to feel like a considered collectible, with believable surface wear and controlled detail at a small scale.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: I studied shipping containers, industrial labeling, street infrastructure, and the campaign’s palette. I modeled the container in Fusion 360, then developed its textures, graffiti, and weathering before printing and hand-finishing the object.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Muted green, black, white, and brown establish a restrained palette. Song and collaborator text takes the role of industrial labeling, while limited graffiti and worn edges connect the object to the gritty atmosphere of its references.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This NVIDIA drop concept focuses on the journey from entering a release to completing a purchase. The design prioritizes clear status, availability, and next steps for someone making decisions under time pressure.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The challenge was communicating enough information without adding clutter to the purchase flow. Queue position, stock status, connection problems, time limits, and completion states all needed to remain clear and consistent.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Journey maps, a sitemap, logic mapping, sketches, and wireframes established the flow. Revisions developed the buying sequence alongside success, sold-out, timeout, and connection states, with related dark and light interface treatments.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: NVIDIA’s green and black provide the foundation, with additional tones for depth and state changes. Sharp forms, strong hierarchy, and restrained interaction feedback support a fast, direct visual character across mobile and tablet layouts.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This app redesign follows a video-download journey from choosing a source through downloading and finding the saved file. The supplied brief focuses on making one user journey clearer and more intuitive.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The goal was to connect the app’s actions into an understandable sequence while keeping the library easy to navigate. Source selection, download options, progress, completion, and errors all form part of that journey.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Hand-drawn screen studies and a sitemap established the structure before high-fidelity screens developed the interface. The final folder includes related views for signing in, the library, folders, download settings, completion, and export.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: Consistent navigation and repeated screen structures connect the individual actions. The finished screens present the selected journey as a coherent interface, with a shared style guide supporting the visual language.

sections.heading: OVERVIEW
sections.text: This packaging concept develops a family of coffee and tea packs for Penelope’s. Brand analysis in the project materials emphasizes warmth, shared experiences, and a relaxed atmosphere as the direction for the work.

sections.heading: CHALLENGES & GOALS
sections.text: The packaging needed to connect different products through a common structure while giving each origin or variety a distinct place. The flat artwork also had to account for how the panels meet when the package is assembled.

sections.heading: RESEARCH & ITERATIONS
sections.text: Brand analysis and fieldwork informed sketches and packaging studies. Dieline-based layouts explored how the logo, product information, origin imagery, and supporting messages could move around the folded form.

sections.heading: SOLUTION WITH AESTHETICS
sections.text: A repeated turquoise field and related supporting colors connect the range. Map-based graphics distinguish the products, while the illustrated marks and shared type treatments preserve a recognizable family across coffee and tea.
